purpose: Make interfaces physical, contextual, damageable parts of the world. The same semantic action can be expressed through VR hand motion, an FPS interaction, a physical control, or an accessibility/input binding, while the simulation resolves one consistent action and its consequences.

layers.responsibility: Physical panel, switch, lever, grip, socket, screen, connector, logger port, harness, latch, or tool with identity, location, affordances, condition and access rules.
Intent such as press, pull, rotate, hold, release, inspect, connect, record, isolate, lock, tag, or acknowledge.
Maps VR tracking, FPS reach/use, mouse, keyboard, controller, or accessibility input to the same semantic action.
Resolves reach, posture, force, timing, qualification, fatigue, injury, restraint and Gesture variance.
Applies the action to the target's actual state, interlocks, damage, power, authority and operating conditions.
Records action, actor, target, time, preconditions, outcome, interruption, and consequences for replay, maintenance, audit and contested history.

rules: A key binding may animate the actor's hand to a valid control and drive the same action pipeline as VR hand tracking; it must not bypass reach, occupancy, interlocks, fatigue or target state.
The actor must visibly reach, grasp, press, pull, turn, hold or release the relevant object unless the action is explicitly remote.
Input source changes how intent is expressed, not what the world action means.
A panel can be unpowered, broken, jammed, locked out, unauthorized, misconfigured or physically inaccessible.
A control's response depends on the installed system and operating context; a lever is not globally a generic open/close command.
A damaged screen may become unreadable; a damaged switch may fail open, fail closed, short, jam or become intermittent according to its modeled construction.
Actions are persistent events; retries do not erase earlier attempts or damage.

embodiment.vr: Tracked hands/body, physical reach and posture; optional tracked or simulated harness where safe and available.
embodiment.fps: First-person body/hand representation, reach/use targets, visible grasp and trigger motions; no detached cursor-only actions for physical controls.
embodiment.keyboardAndMouse: Explicit binding to a valid semantic action. For example, forward input can cause the avatar's hand to operate the mech throttle while the control rig moves through a defined range.
embodiment.controller: Direct analog or button input routed through the same action and actor-performance contracts.
embodiment.accessibility: Alternative inputs may replace the physical input gesture but retain authorization, target state, interlocks, and meaningful consequence; accessibility must not be confused with removing physical simulation from NPCs.

breathingGuidance.purpose: A translucent, breathing Gesture ghost demonstrates the expected next action without taking it for the player.
rules: Ghost shows ideal hand/body pose, target, direction, and temporal window.
The ghost breathes the specific control or log port when that control is the next useful action.
Guidance fades or changes when conditions change, a control becomes unsafe, or the player chooses another valid route.
Ghost guidance is not proof that an action is safe; live interlocks and measured state remain authoritative.
Repeated failure may adjust explanation and practice, but must not secretly perform the action.

physicalInterfaces.screen: A physical display surface with power, input source, readability, damage, refresh/latency and access state; content is constrained by what that terminal can know.
physicalInterfaces.lever: A physical travel range, force profile, detents, latch/interlock and return behavior.
physicalInterfaces.trigger: A physical trigger or equivalent control with safe/armed state, authorization, travel and weapon-system response.
physicalInterfaces.loggerPort: A physical interface where the actor removes, carries, aligns and connects a logger. The logger records actual accessible settings and samples with timestamps, units, calibration, gaps and provenance.
physicalInterfaces.motionHarness: A restraint and motion-capture rig that constrains posture and measures movement/force. It has fit, calibration, safety release, fatigue load and maintenance state.
physicalInterfaces.mechControlRig: Grips, pedals, foot plates, harness and switches map to actuator commands through vehicle control laws, power limits, thermal limits, damage and pilot skill; control motion does not directly dictate every actuator one-to-one.

lockoutTagout.principle: Isolation must be physically established, verified, individually locked, tagged, tested, and released through a traceable procedure. The friction is deliberate gameplay and operational realism, not random waiting.
gameplayConsequences: wrong source identification leaves a live hazard
a shared lock box or multi-person isolation prevents one person restoring energy under another worker
stored energy can reaccumulate and require re-verification
missing tags or stale drawings force investigation
emergency bypass is possible only under explicit authority and records a persistent incident
an impatient shortcut can injure workers, damage equipment, invalidate qualification or trigger an inquiry
noMagicRules: A UI checkbox does not isolate a physical energy source.
An unverified indicator is not proof of zero energy.
A tag communicates identity and intent but does not physically prevent energization; the lock/interlock does that job.
The simulation must model credible sources, isolation points, verification instruments and stored-energy paths, not turn every job into identical busywork.

validationGates: Same action semantics across VR/FPS/mouse/keyboard/controller adapters.
Input binding cannot bypass physical target state, authorization or interlocks.
Guidance ghost never executes the action.
Every completed or failed interaction can be tied to a persistent event.
Logger records accessible measurements and provenance, not hidden omniscient truth.
Damage can alter interaction affordances and downstream function.
Motion harness has safety release, fit and calibration states.
Lockout/tagout cannot be completed without isolation, lock, verification, work-clearance and restoration evidence.
